reasoning_traces.think:
The core mechanism of verifiable reward calibration hinges on minimizing the Brier score, which is strictly proper and uniquely minimized by the true conditional probability η(x) = Pr(win|x). The reward function r = 1 - (p - p̂(x))² incentivizes alignment between predicted probability p and empirical rate p̂. This setup ensures that even without access to realized outcomes during training, the model learns to produce well-calibrated forecasts. In GSE, this translates to optimizing state transitions using a calibrated probability distribution derived from historical picks. The empirical rate teacher provides a stable reference, mitigating overfitting to small datasets. Masked chain-of-thought reasoning further enhances calibration by isolating the final probability output from potentially noisy reasoning steps. The failure mode arises when reasoning tokens introduce inconsistent gradients, causing decalibration—this is addressed by masking reasoning tokens and focusing gradients on the final output span.
